I'll start by reading the docs and the existing code.

The unfinished parts are `evaluate`, `pattern_text`, grouping in `number_text`, the CSV writer (it uses CRLF-less `csv` quoting), null placement in the sort, and `part_paths`. I'll fix each of them.

I'll make the edits one at a time, starting with the CSV writer.

Next is `text.py`, using file edits.

The `export` command is finished and follows `docs/export.md`. The full suite passes (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, 28 tests, OK). I also ran a few exports by hand against `/app/store`. The `--where` operators and several sort and quoting cases weren't exercised by hand; the suite doesn't cover them, so I didn't test them.

I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

What I fixed or added, all under `/app/tally`:
- **`--where`:** `evaluate` in `export/expr.py` was missing. Nulls make every comparison, `in` and `not in` false, and `not` flips the result.
- **`--sort`:** `nulls-first` and `nulls-last` were being flipped by `:desc`. Now an explicit placement holds in either direction. Without one, nulls still sort as larger than every value.
- **Locale numbers and dates:**
  - Digit grouping now uses the locale's `group_sizes` and `min_grouping`, and `--no-grouping` turns it off. The old code grouped in threes only.
  - Date and datetime patterns now use the longest-token-first rule from section 7.4, including the 12-hour clock and `A` for AM/PM.
- **CSV text:** the old code used Python's `csv` module, which didn't give CRLF line ends or the quoting rules in section 8.4. I replaced it with a writer that implements them. Null values are written as the bare null token. Text equal to the null token is quoted, so empty strings become `""` with the default token.
- **`--max-rows`:** file naming now takes the suffix from the last `.` and treats a leading dot as part of the name (`.x` becomes `.x-001`). The sequence number has three digits, or more when the last file's number needs them.

I did not change anything under `/app/tests`, `/app/store`, `/app/locales` or `/app/docs`.
